call_points.text: Retail health growth guided at 8-10 percentage points faster than market
Expense of management ratio expected to stabilise at 32-33%
Retail/group mix expected to stay around 70/30
Board approved debt raising committee and enabling resolution for up to ₹500 Cr
₹250 Cr NCD call option due this year; issuer rating AAA by ICRA
Solvency 2.25 at 30 June 2026 against regulatory minimum 1.50
Retail health grew 47.1% reported; group book flat on pricing
Preferred provider network claims cost 15-30% lower than tertiary care for like treatments
Management expects industry retail health growth to sustain at 17% to 19% CAGR over a 5-year view.
The combined operating ratio under IFRS is targeted to reach around 99% by FY29, translating to mid-to-high teens ROE.
Solvency ratio stood at a healthy 2.49 as of March 31, 2026.
Retail Health market share reached 10.1% in FY26 compared to 9.4% in FY25.
IRDAI has mandated Ind AS financial reporting effective April 01, 2026, aligning reporting standards with global practices.

guidance.statement: Industry retail health growth is expected to be at 17% to 19% CAGR over a 5-year view.
Retail health growth 8-10 percentage points faster than market
ROE mid to high teens by FY29
Expense of management ratio to stabilise at 32-33%

operating_notes.text: Q4FY26 combined ratio of 86.12% was the first below 100% in memory, against 108.19% in Q3FY26 and 111.72% in Q2FY26.
FY26 incurred claims rose 37.9% to ₹4,132.58 Cr, faster than net premium's 26.8%, lifting the full-year claims ratio to 68.11% from 61.22%.
Solvency ratio fell to 2.49 at March 31, 2026 from 3.03 a year earlier.
AUM grew 18.3% YoY to ₹9,669.7 Cr in FY26 with an investment yield of 7.2%.
Active lives insured expanded to 25.2 million in FY26 from 20.8 million in FY25.
Cashless claims auto-adjudication reached 32.1% on an exit basis in FY26.
FY26 retail health growth for Niva Bupa exceeded 40% in H2, driven by GST tailwinds and distribution expansion.
Retail health fresh business is about 35% and renewal about 65% of retail premium.
Preferred provider network covers 49 cities and over 1,000 hospitals, with 22% of claims flowing through it.
AIF investments are about 4% of AUM with 12-15% yields; Nifty ETF exposure is around 3.5% of the investment book.
The 10.70% NCDs (1,500 of ₹10 lakh each, ₹150 Cr) were allotted 15 November 2021 and are being called at the first call date, 15 November 2026, paid on 13 November 2026.
India Ratings assigned IND AAA/Stable to ₹500 Cr of proposed subordinated NCDs, marked yet to be issued.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹1,971.95 Cr (+29.1% YoY), net profit ₹345.13 Cr (+67.5% YoY).
Niva Bupa released its FY26 investor presentation reporting GWP of ₹9,432.9 Cr (+27.4% YoY) and IFRS PAT of ₹366.1 Cr (+80.4% YoY).
Niva Bupa Health Insurance reported FY26 IFRS PAT of ₹366 crore on May 8, 2026.
Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited hosted an earnings call on May 08, 2026, discussing Q4FY26 and FY26 performance, with recording available at transactions.nivabupa.com.
On May 13, 2026, Niva Bupa filed the earnings call transcript for its Q4 and FY26 financial results held on May 8, 2026.
Niva Bupa's Q1FY27 earnings call reported PAT of ₹137.8 Cr, CISR improving 300 bps to 100.2%, and a board enabling resolution to raise up to ₹500 Cr of debt.
On 15 October 2026, Niva Bupa dispatched a call option notice to redeem its ₹150 Cr 10.70% NCDs at par on 13 November 2026, stating post-call solvency will stay above 180%.
On 15 October 2026, India Ratings assigned IND AAA/Stable to Niva Bupa's proposed ₹500 Cr subordinated NCDs, which are yet to be issued.
